body.statement: For sample sizes in the deterministic eventual regime \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\ge T_0\), uniformly over observed laws \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_n/\mathcal V(P)\to1\) and \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}\Pr_P(\widehat T_n\ge T_0)\to1\). On \(\{\widehat T_n\ge T_0\}\), \(b(\widehat T_n)-b(T_n(P))=o_P(a(T_n(P)))\) and \(a(\widehat T_n)/a(T_n(P))\to1\). Hence the eventual-regime analytic critical value \(\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\), built from the exact Palm-intensity expansion, and the canonical-simulation critical value \(\widehat q^{\mathrm{sim}}_{n,\alpha}\), built from \(n^2\) copies of the prescribed padded grid target, satisfy \(\Pr_P\{S_n(\theta)\le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\}\to1-\alpha\) and \(\Pr_P\{S_n(\theta)\le\widehat q^{\mathrm{sim}}_{n,\alpha}\}\to1-\alpha\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\); both critical values equal \(+\infty\) on the vanishing complement \(\{\widehat T_n<T_0\}\).
body.justification: Pointwise pivotality does not remove the population-dependent number of effective LR opportunities, so the spatial clock must be estimated at the centering scale.
body.gap: Takatsu and Westling (2025) estimate ingredients for Gaussian uniform bands, and Westling, Gilbert, and Carone (2020) study a pointwise isotonic scale; neither propagates a plug-in LR clock through Gumbel centering.
body.consumer: Clock substitution calculus is conditional; nominal feasible calibration is not established.

obligation.what_is_open: Nominal analytic and simulated calibration remains conditional on uniform clock consistency, the canonical Gumbel law, observed-law transfer, random-horizon padded-grid approximation, and quantile anti-concentration.
obligation.obstruction: Relative clock consistency would justify substitution into an already established centering and scale, but it cannot create the missing limit law or identify finite padded-simulation quantiles with continuum quantiles.
obligation.attempted: The uniform positive lower bound for the spatial volume, inverse-centering mean-value calculation, asymptotic scale substitution, and conditional empirical-distribution error for the prescribed number of simulations were derived.
obligation.partial_result:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(\texttt{ass:p-normalization}\), \(\texttt{ass:overlap}\), \(\texttt{ass:strict-slope}\), and \(\texttt{ass:variance}\) imply
\[
 \mathcal V(P)
 \ge |J|\left\{\frac{c_gc_\theta^2}{4V_\kappa}\right\}^{1/3}>0.
\]
Hence \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\to\infty\), so the deterministic eventual regime is nonempty for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Conditional on the still-unproved uniform clock consistency
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal V}_n/\mathcal V(P)=1+o_P(1),
\]
one has \(\log\{\widehat T_n/T_n(P)\}=o_P(1)\) and \(\Pr_P\{\widehat T_n\ge T_0\}\to1\) uniformly.  On that event, the mean-value theorem applied to \(\mathcal E_\star(b(T))=\log T\) gives
\[
 \frac{b(\widehat T_n)-b(T_n(P))}{a(T_n(P))}
 =\frac{\mathcal E_\star'(b(T_n(P)))}
        {\mathcal E_\star'(\widetilde b_n)}
   \log\frac{\widehat T_n}{T_n(P)},
\]
where \(\widetilde b_n\) lies between the two centerings.  If the canonical expansion asserted by \(\texttt{thm:canonical-excursion}\) were available, then both centerings would diverge and
\[
 \mathcal E_\star'(u)=\beta_\star+\frac{\gamma_\star}{u},
 \qquad
 \frac{b(\widehat T_n)-b(T_n(P))}{a(T_n(P))}=o_P(1),
\]
while
\[
 \frac{a(\widehat T_n)}{a(T_n(P))}
 =\frac{\mathcal E_\star'(b(T_n(P)))}
        {\mathcal E_\star'(b(\widehat T_n))}
 \longrightarrow1.
\]
Thus clock substitution is valid once the missing expansion and clock consistency have been proved.  Conditionally on the data, the Dvoretzky--Kiefer--Wolfowitz bound for the prescribed \(n^2\) independent simulated maxima yields uniform empirical-distribution error \(O_P(n^{-1})\).  That empirical bound alone supplies neither the random-horizon padded-grid approximation nor the anti-concentration needed to transfer simulated quantiles to the continuum maximum.
